newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' debt burden to weigh on credit grade.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' debt burden to weigh on credit grade.

text.p: The Philippines' high debt burden would go against the country during a review of its sovereign rating by international agencies, Hendrick Kranenburg, executive vice president of Standard & Poor's told reporters over the weekend.
Following the signing of an important tax reform bill last Friday, government officials said a credit upgrade is possible next year.
The Philippines was last upgraded in May 1995. Its rating is Double-B, two steps away from the investment grade rating of Triple-B Minus.
"It's also important to remember that the country remains highly indebted.. (the) high debt burden remains a constraining factor," Kranenburg said.

According to S&P data published in May 1996, the national government's net debt as a percentage of gross domestic product was 34 percent in 1996. Its net debt in relation to exports was 82 percent in 1996.
Kranenburg said the Philippines' low savings rate was also a concern but they were encouraged by the country's lower inflation and good fiscal position.
New York-based Kranenburg was in Manila to attend the meetings the APEC Business Forum.
Data compiled by the Asian Development Bank showed the Philippines had the lowest savings rate at 15 percent of gross domestic product compared with the average of over 30 percent within the region.
